name: Wilbur Clearing Appalachian Trail Primitive Campsite - Mount Greylock

management_agency.name: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) / ATC

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fee or permit required for primitive trail camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 1 night stay limit for hikers along Appalachian Trail
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Primitive camping permitted only at designated AT campsites/shelters within Mount Greylock State Reservation. Leave No Trace mandatory.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Use on-site wooden privy; otherwise dig cat-hole 6-8 inches deep in forest soil, at least 200 feet from streams. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out. Black bears present: food storage container or bear hang required.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Massachusetts DCR burn bans during dry periods.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state road to trailhead parking (Notch Road) followed by 1.0 mile walk-in trail
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Paved mountain road leading to trailhead parking lot. Campsite is walk-in / hike-in.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (parked at trailhead lot)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 3-4 bars 5G/LTE (25-50 Mbps download on high mountain clearing)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (High elevation clearing near Mount Greylock summit ridge)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 45-60°F, high snowmelt runoff, muddy trails, chilly nights.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 70-80°F, pleasant mountain temperature, shaded northern hardwood canopy.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: World-class Berkshires autumn leaf foliage (50-65°F daytime, 30-40°F nights), crisp clear skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cold mountain winter (15-30°F), heavy snowpack, Notch Road closed to motor vehicles (cross-country ski trail).

dangers_and_hazards: Black Bears active along AT corridor - bear hang or canister required

common_human_made_sounds: Distant town sounds from North Adams valley (3 miles away)

human_demographics_and_culture: Appalachian Trail thru-hikers, Williams College students, Berkshires digital nomads, and autumn leaf peepers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Mahican indigenous traditions revere Mount Greylock ('Grandfather Mountain') as the sacred highest peak in the Berkshires, holding ancient sky spirit wisdom.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: High elevation mountain peak energy, rich Berkshires literary inspiration (Melville, Thoreau), 5G connected wilderness.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Appalachian Trail - Mount Greylock Summit Section
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Ascent to highest peak in Massachusetts (3,491 ft) with Veterans War Memorial Tower

public_reviews_summary: Fantastic high-elevation primitive trail camping near Mount Greylock. High-speed 5G cell internet and great mountain views.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Short walk-in access.
